problem: the effect-class registry pinned subprocess.run call sites by LINE NUMBER through _LEGACY_LINE_REMAP. The remap maps 'current line at pin time' -> 'legacy line', so its KEYS go stale on any later edit and it can never heal. Measured: a +1 line insertion in astra_runtime.py moved every site (400->401, 862->863, ...) while the keys stayed put, so nothing matched and the gate raised LEGACY_VERIFIED_SITE_DISAPPEARED, making NINE test files uncollectable.
three_failed_attempts_before_the_working: v1: resolve the stale line through _norm_key, then parse the current source for the enclosing function. Failed because _norm_key maps CURRENT->LEGACY (feeding it a legacy line returns it unchanged), and one of the six sites is at MODULE level so a function-keyed lookup cannot resolve it.
v2: match on (module, api, function) with ambiguity refusing. Failed for the same reason -- the function was still being looked up through the stale line.

v3 (working): re-derive the current->legacy correspondence at COMPILE TIME by pairing the module's current sites with its legacy pins IN ORDER, and only when the counts agree. Count agrees => correspondence exact, drift harmless. Count differs => a call was genuinely added or removed and the original refusal stands.

plus a fourth bug in v3: the derived remap was computed but the row builder still read the static one, so the failure simply moved to LEGACY_PRESERVATION_COUNT_MISMATCH. Fixed by feeding the derived pairs back into _LEGACY_LINE_REMAP.
principle: the obligation a pin encodes is 'this module makes N calls to this API, each with a verified effect class'. It does NOT encode an address. Prove the obligation, not the address.

verification.clean_tree: compile OK, only benign identity remaps reported
verification.drift_probe: inserting one line at astra_runtime.py:3 -> previously FAILED with LEGACY_VERIFIED_SITE_DISAPPEARED, now SELF-HEALED OK
verification.regression: 47 passed across strict bootstrap v1/v2, two-class authorizer, subprocess mediator, closed-loop repair spec, input-dependency gate

scope_limit: the count must match. Adding or removing a subprocess.run site in a pinned module is still a refusal, by design -- that is a real change to the process universe, not drift.
